_about: The numbered parts on a chapter's specimen drawing, keyed by chapter id (the owner's decisions of 25 Oct 2026, Lithography, and 29 Oct 2026, Silicon and Wafers, Memory and HBM and Advanced Packaging, from the labels mockup; add a chapter only from a sourced list). Each part has its number (n), its name, the shorter name its label on the drawing carries where the list's name is long (label), and either its maker as the chapter's card and text source it (maker, with link: [href, words] where a section of the chapter covers it) or the chapter that covers it (stage, a chapter id, shown as 'see stage NN, Title'). Where a part has no maker of its own, maker is a short phrase from the chapter's text (approved by the owner, 29 Oct 2026). build/build.js draws the list under the specimen's caption. Foundries and Fabs and the fifth part of Advanced Packaging were added on 22 Nov 2026 from the parts chapter 8 and chapter 10 name. Since 21 Nov 2026 the specimen is an exploded technical plate (src/plate.js, plates/<specimen>.js): its numbered labels take their names from here (label, else name), and the part each lights is set in the plate's model to match the part's light table. 'light' lists the shapes the point-cloud drawing lit when the reader pointed at a part, in the old specimen's own units (specimens/<specimen>.js): a rod from one point to another with its radius (r), a ball round a point (r), or a box between two corners; soft is the width of the edge over which the light falls off; only keeps it to the ink or the accent points, which the plate reads too; layers [y, pitch, half] keeps it to thin layers. 'at' lists the points the old drawing's balloon pointed at, in the same units, kept as the record of where each part is. On 25 Nov 2026 the parts of ten more chapters were added (Chip Design, EDA and IP; Chemicals, Gases and Photoresist; Photomasks and Pellicles; Deposition and Etch; Metrology and Inspection; Substrates and PCBs; Test and Assembly; Systems and Networking; Data Centers and Power; and The Economics of AI Chips), and Advanced Packaging's fifth part now names TSMC, all at the final text of that day's expert and fact-check pass on the parts reviews. Each of those lists is numbered top to bottom as its labels stand on the drawing (two labels level with each other read left, then right), a maker is named only where the chapter's text sources it, and a link may point at a ### subsection as well as a section.
